name: Pacific & Indian cyclones
summary: Cyclone Murasu weakens inland after Andhra Pradesh landfall; GDACS red alert still listed
state: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole early on 3 Nov with winds of 100–110km/h and was forecast to weaken overnight. State officials reported two deaths in Bapatla district, 312 houses damaged, 52,459 hectares of crops hit and 12,230 people moved to relief centres (The News Minute, 4 Nov). GDACS still listed a red alert on 4 Nov.
for_you: Follow India Meteorological Department and FCDO advice if travelling in Andhra Pradesh or Telangana.

sources.title: The News Minute — Cyclone Murasu leaves 2 dead, damages 312 houses in Andhra Pradesh

why: Typhoons and cyclones are the deadliest weather events, threatening densely populated coasts in Asia and the Indian Ocean.
drivers: Ocean heat, ENSO phase, season (W Pacific peaks Jul–Oct; N Indian Apr–Jun & Oct–Dec).

rubric.alert: GDACS red cyclone alert, or a super-typhoon/severe cyclone landfall on a populated coast.
rubric.watch: GDACS orange cyclone alert, or a typhoon/cyclone threatening land within 72h.
rubric.normal: No GDACS orange/red tropical cyclone alerts.
